name: Studio Be
description: Brandan "BMike" Odums' massive warehouse gallery in the Bywater. 35,000 sq ft of large-scale murals and installations exploring Black American identity. Powerful stuff.
must_try: The massive spray-painted portraits — they stop you in your tracks

name: Sydney & Walda Besthoff Sculpture Garden
description: Spectacular free 12-acre outdoor installation with 90+ modern sculptures among winding lagoons and 200-year-old live oaks. One of the best free attractions in any American city.
must_try: The reflecting lagoons and the giant spider sculpture

name: Longue Vue House and Gardens
description: Stunning Classical Revival estate with eight acres of interactive gardens. A peaceful escape from the city energy.
must_try: Guided house tour followed by coffee at the Garden Café

name: Jackson Square
description: The heart of the French Quarter. St. Louis Cathedral as the backdrop, street performers, tarot readers, artists selling paintings on the iron fence. Free to walk through.
must_try: Walk through in the morning before the crowds, or at dusk when the light hits the cathedral

name: St. Louis Cathedral
address: 615 Pere Antoine Alley, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: The oldest continuously active cathedral in the United States. The interior is stunning and it's free to visit.
must_try: Step inside even for 5 minutes — the painted ceiling and stained glass are incredible

name: Aquarium of the Americas
description: World-class riverfront facility with immersive Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean reef habitats. The shark and ray exhibit is massive.
must_try: Gulf of Mexico shark and ray exhibit

name: Backstreet Cultural Museum
address: 1531 St Philip St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Profoundly important Tremé institution preserving Mardi Gras Indian traditions, jazz funeral culture, and Black social aid clubs. Essential for understanding real New Orleans.
must_try: The elaborately hand-beaded Mardi Gras Indian suits

name: Historic Voodoo Museum
description: Small, casual museum packed floor-to-ceiling with artifacts preserving New Orleans Voodoo history. Leave an offering at Marie Laveau's altar.
must_try: Offering at the altar of Marie Laveau

name: New Orleans Museum of Art (NOMA)
address: 1 Collins Diboll Cir, New Orleans, LA 70124
description: City Park's anchor museum with 40,000+ works spanning 5,000 years. Free on Wednesdays for Louisiana residents. The adjacent Sculpture Garden is free daily.
must_try: The photography galleries and the free Sculpture Garden next door

name: New Orleans Pharmacy Museum
description: Fascinating look at 19th-century medicine, voodoo remedies, and surgical oddities in America's first licensed apothecary.
must_try: Guided tour of historical medical practices

name: Ogden Museum of Southern Art
description: The largest collection of Southern art in the world. Ogden After Hours on Thursday nights: live music, cocktails, and gallery access for $10.
must_try: Ogden After Hours — Thursday 6-8pm, live music + cocktails + galleries, $10

name: The Cabildo
description: Elegant Spanish colonial building next to St. Louis Cathedral where the Louisiana Purchase was transferred. Napoleon's death mask is here.
must_try: Napoleon's death mask and the Battle of New Orleans exhibits

name: The National WWII Museum
description: The #1 attraction in New Orleans and consistently rated the best museum in America. You need 4-5 hours minimum. The Beyond All Boundaries film narrated by Tom Hanks is worth it alone.
must_try: Beyond All Boundaries 4D film, the submarine exhibit, Stage Door Canteen dinner show

name: The Presbytère
description: Twin of the Cabildo, brilliantly chronicling Mardi Gras history and the impact of Hurricane Katrina. The interactive float exhibits are fantastic.
must_try: Interactive Mardi Gras float exhibits

name: Garden District Walking Tour
address: Start at Washington Ave & Prytania St, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Self-guided or with a tour company. Antebellum mansions, Lafayette Cemetery No. 1, Anne Rice's former home, Sandra Bullock's house. Free to walk on your own.
must_try: Walk Prytania and Coliseum streets. Stop at Lafayette Cemetery No. 1.

name: Mardi Gras World
address: 1380 Port of New Orleans Pl, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Massive working warehouse where artists build the spectacular floats for the city's largest parades, year-round. Watch the styrofoam carving process up close.
must_try: Watching the float-building process and trying on costumes

name: St. Charles Streetcar
address: St. Charles Ave (Canal to Carrollton), New Orleans, LA 70130
description: The oldest continuously operating streetcar in the world (1835). Ride the full line from Canal through the Garden District to Audubon Park for $1.25. Better than any bus tour.
must_try: Ride the full line one way — sit on the right side heading Uptown for the best mansion views

name: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1
description: The city's oldest and most famous above-ground cemetery. Must visit with a licensed tour guide — no unguided entry allowed.
must_try: Tomb of Voodoo Queen Marie Laveau and Nicolas Cage's pyramid tomb
hours: Guided tours only, varies by operator

name: Steamboat Natchez
address: Toulouse St Wharf, 400 Toulouse St, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: The last authentic steamboat on the Mississippi. Jazz brunch cruise and evening dinner cruise with live music. Touristy? Sure. But being on the river with a brass band hits different.
must_try: The jazz brunch cruise on Sunday

name: Tremé Neighborhood Walking Tour
description: Essential historical deep-dive into America's oldest African-American neighborhood — the birthplace of jazz, Congo Square, and the cradle of local civil rights.
must_try: Visiting Congo Square

name: Bayou Beer Garden
address: 326 N Jefferson Davis Pkwy, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Massive Mid-City beer garden with 40+ taps, food trucks, and a chill outdoor vibe. Great for watching games and afternoon drinks.
must_try: Local craft beer flights, whatever food truck is parked outside

name: Courtyard Brewery
description: Pioneering micro-brewery with an eclectic open-air taproom. West Coast IPAs and experimental Saisons in a chill Lower Garden District setting.
must_try: Rotating hop-forward IPAs

name: NOLA Brewing
description: Local brewery taproom near the river. Good beer, casual vibe, food trucks on weekends. The NOLA Blonde is everywhere in the city.
must_try: NOLA Blonde, Irish Channel Stout, or whatever's on the seasonal tap

name: Parleaux Beer Lab
description: Destination Bywater micro-brewery with an expansive outdoor beer garden and imaginative small-batch brews. The sour ales are stellar.
must_try: Rotating fruit-infused sour ales

name: Port Orleans Brewing Co.
description: Sprawling brewery and beer garden with clean lagers and ales. Spring crawfish boils on the patio are legendary.
must_try: Spring crawfish boils and their flagship lager

name: Urban South Brewery
description: Sprawling Tchoupitoulas brewery with a massive taproom, food trucks, and a family-friendly beer garden. The Holy Roller IPA is their flagship.
must_try: Holy Roller IPA and whatever food truck is posted up

name: Bar Tonique
address: 820 N Rampart St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: The bartenders' bar. No-nonsense craft cocktails on the edge of the Quarter. This is where industry people drink after their shifts.
must_try: Ask for a dealer's choice cocktail — the bartenders here are world-class

name: Compère Lapin Bar
description: The impeccable bar inside Chef Nina Compton's flagship restaurant. Gulf-Caribbean cocktails in one of the most beautiful hotel bar spaces in the city.
must_try: The Copper Bunny cocktail

name: Cure
description: The cocktail bar that launched the Freret Street revival. James Beard-nominated. Gorgeous converted firehouse. Serious drinks, zero pretension.
must_try: Any of the rotating seasonal cocktails — the menu changes constantly

name: Pat O'Brien's
address: 718 St Peter St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Home of the Hurricane cocktail. Yes, it's touristy. Yes, you should go once. The flaming fountain courtyard and dueling piano bar are legitimately fun.
must_try: Hurricane cocktail in the courtyard by the flaming fountain

name: Sazerac Bar
address: 130 Roosevelt Way (The Roosevelt Hotel), New Orleans, LA 70112
description: Art Deco palace where you drink the city's namesake cocktail. The Sazerac was created nearby in the 1800s. This is the definitive place to drink one.
must_try: A Sazerac. Obviously.

name: The Carousel Bar & Lounge
description: The only revolving bar in New Orleans, inside the Hotel Monteleone. The bar literally turns as you drink. A Vieux Carré cocktail here is mandatory.
must_try: Vieux Carré cocktail (invented at the Hotel Monteleone)

name: The Elysian Bar
description: Inside Hotel Peter and Paul's converted church. Stained glass, vaulted ceilings, gorgeous cocktails. Open to non-guests. The most beautiful bar in the city.
must_try: Any seasonal cocktail in the main church room

name: Three Muses
description: Music, food, and drinks — all three at a high level in a tiny Frenchmen Street space. Small plates, craft cocktails, live jazz nightly.
must_try: Korean-influenced small plates while listening to live jazz

name: Aunt Tiki's
description: Famously gritty 24/7 punk rock dive on the edge of the Quarter. Strong drinks, eclectic late-night crowd. Not for the faint of heart.
must_try: A strong mixed drink at 4am

name: Lafitte's Blacksmith Shop Bar
description: Built between 1722-1732, it's the oldest structure used as a bar in America. Candlelit, no neon, all atmosphere. The one Bourbon Street bar every local respects.
must_try: Purple drink (frozen grape), sit in the candlelit back room

name: Pal's Lounge
address: 949 N Rendon St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Quintessential Mid-City neighborhood bar. Incredibly welcoming with great pop-up food vendors and famous air conditioning.
must_try: Ginger-infused vodka cocktail

name: Saturn Bar
address: 3067 St Claude Ave, New Orleans, LA 70117
description: Iconic eclectically decorated St. Claude dive known for its artsy crowd, stellar jukebox, and epic weekend dance parties.
must_try: Cheap beer during a weekend DJ set

name: Snake & Jake's Christmas Club Lounge
description: The most legendary dive in New Orleans — a pitch-dark shack on Oak Street draped in permanent Christmas lights. Opens at midnight, closes when they feel like it. No sign, no pretense, no equal.
must_try: Cheap beer in the dark. That's the whole experience.

name: St. Joe's Bar
description: Atmospheric dimly lit Uptown bar with religious iconography and one of the most pleasant courtyards in the city.
must_try: Blueberry mojito in the courtyard

name: The Dungeon
description: Legendary dark rock-and-roll dive hidden down a French Quarter alleyway. A late-night rite of passage since 1969.
must_try: Dragon's Blood cocktail

name: Twelve Mile Limit
address: 500 S Telemachus St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Mid-City dive that secretly serves world-class craft cocktails at neighborhood prices with nightly local food pop-ups. The best-kept-secret bar in the city.
must_try: The $5 Bee's Knees special

name: Blue Nile
description: The original Frenchmen Street music club — funk, brass, soul in an 1832 building. Two stages, upstairs balcony overlooking the street. Many shows are free.
must_try: Check the upstairs late-night DJ sets and the balcony view

name: Chickie Wah Wah
description: Intimate Mid-City music room showcasing premier local roots, blues, and Americana. The weeknight residencies are where locals go.
must_try: A weeknight residency show

name: Civic Theatre
description: The oldest theater in New Orleans with a stunning high-tech modular floor and spectacular acoustics for major touring acts.
must_try: Standing room near the stage

name: Fritzel's European Jazz Pub
description: The oldest operating jazz club in New Orleans, hiding in plain sight on Bourbon Street. One-drink minimum. Real jazz in a sea of karaoke and cover bands.
must_try: Duck in from Bourbon Street — the contrast between Fritzel's and everything around it is stunning

name: Gasa Gasa
description: Artsy eclectic indie music venue anchoring the Freret corridor. Known for discovering underground talent. Great courtyard art installations.
must_try: Courtyard art between sets

name: Joy Theater
description: Restored 1947 Art Deco movie house turned premier concert and comedy venue on Canal Street. Gorgeous room.
must_try: Comedy tour or indie rock show

name: Kermit's Tremé Mother-in-Law Lounge
address: 1500 N Claiborne Ave, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Kermit Ruffins' backyard party. Pay your cover at the back door and walk into a legendary barbecue-and-brass-band scene. The real Tremé experience.
must_try: Go on a Monday — Kermit often plays himself. Eat whatever he's barbecuing.

name: Mahogany Jazz Hall
description: Intimate Frenchmen Street jazz venue. Just a one-drink minimum per set. Solid traditional jazz in a cozy, dark space.
must_try: Weeknight sets — smaller crowds, incredible musicians

name: Preservation Hall
address: 726 St Peter St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Nightly traditional jazz in a 250-year-old French Quarter room with no A/C, no drinks, and no frills — just the purest jazz experience on earth. Shows at 5pm, 6pm, 8pm, 9pm, 10pm.
must_try: The 8pm or 9pm show. Line up 30 min early for bench seats.

name: Republic NOLA
address: 828 S Peters St, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Massive converted Arts District warehouse with crystal chandeliers hosting major touring EDM, hip-hop, and bounce acts.
must_try: VIP balcony for major DJ sets

name: Snug Harbor Jazz Bistro
description: The serious jazz club on Frenchmen. Cabaret-style seating, Marsalis family regulars, Creole food in the bistro. Cover charge for the music room but worth every cent.
must_try: Book a table for dinner in the Bistro, then catch the 8pm or 10pm show

name: The Fillmore New Orleans
description: State-of-the-art concert hall on the second floor of Harrah's Casino. Premium national touring acts on the riverfront.
must_try: Pre-show drinks in BG's Lounge

name: The Maison
description: The biggest venue on Frenchmen. Multiple stages, VIP tables, jazz + dinner, drag shows upstairs on weekends, and a mixology class you can book.
must_try: Reserve a premium table for dinner + jazz, or catch the Wig Snatchers drag show Fri/Sat 8pm upstairs

name: The Spotted Cat Music Club
description: The single best bar in New Orleans, according to just about every local. Cash only, no cover, incredible bands every night, everyone dancing. The floor of Frenchmen Street.
must_try: Show up by 8pm to get a spot. Cash only — ATM before you go.

name: Tipitina's
description: The legendary Uptown music hall named after a Professor Longhair song. National touring acts and local legends. If you only go to one ticketed show, make it Tip's.
must_try: Check the calendar — it's the best live music room in the city

name: Toulouse Theatre
description: Revived independent French Quarter music venue carrying the torch of NOLA's 1970s music scene. Late-night brass band throwdowns.
must_try: Late-night brass band sets

name: d.b.a.
description: Sleek dark wood interior, the best craft beer selection on Frenchmen, and acts like Tremé Brass Band and Corey Henry. The musicians' bar.
must_try: Grab a local craft beer and catch whoever's on stage — it's always good

name: Fives
address: 529 St Ann St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: An intimate cocktail lounge and raw bar in the historic Pontalba Buildings on Jackson Square. Gulf and East Coast oysters, caviar, and incredible cocktails under an antique chandelier.
must_try: Saturn in Retrograde cocktail paired with Gulf Coast oysters

name: Bacchanal Fine Wine & Spirits
description: The most romantic spot in the city. Pick wine from the front shop, grab cheese and charcuterie, then sit in the twinkling courtyard with live jazz under the trees. Bywater magic.
must_try: Build your own wine and cheese plate, then sit in the courtyard at sunset

name: Effervescence
address: 1036 N Rampart St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Elegant champagne bar on the edge of the Quarter with chef-inspired sharing plates and premium bubbles.
must_try: Half-shell oysters paired with a sparkling wine flight

name: N7
description: Transportive French wine bar hidden behind a wooden fence in the Bywater. Natural wines, canned sardines, and a cinematic atmosphere that makes you forget what city you're in.
must_try: Canned European sardines paired with a natural Pét-Nat

name: Haydel's Bakery
description: Legendary multi-generational family bakery famous internationally for Mardi Gras King Cakes. Ships nationwide during Carnival season.
must_try: Traditional braided King Cake or Cajun Kringle

name: La Boulangerie
description: French bakery from the Link Restaurant Group. Flawless laminated pastries, fresh breads, and elevated sandwiches on Magazine Street.
must_try: Almond croissant or Jambon Beurre

name: Loretta's Authentic Pralines
address: 1100 N Peters St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: French Market staple from the first African-American woman to own a praline company in New Orleans. Essential eating.
must_try: Praline-stuffed beignet

name: Sucré
description: Visually stunning dessert boutique on Magazine Street. French macarons, artisanal chocolates, and rich gelatos.
must_try: Macaron collection and shimmering petit fours

name: Café Beignet
description: Atmospheric alternative to Café Du Monde with excellent beignets, live jazz, and charming courtyard seating. Shorter lines.
must_try: Classic beignets and iced café au lait in the courtyard

name: Café Du Monde
description: Open since 1862, serving exactly three things: beignets, café au lait, and orange juice. The line moves fast. Powdered sugar on your shirt is a badge of honor.
must_try: Beignets and café au lait — that's the entire menu. Order 1 plate per person.
hours: Open 24 hours, 7 days a week (closes Christmas Day)

name: Cherry Coffee Roasters
description: Airy, beautifully designed Uptown café with deeply serious locally roasted coffee and exceptional breakfast items.
must_try: Cortado and the breakfast biscuit

name: French Truck Coffee
description: The city's preeminent local specialty roaster with the bright yellow branding. Small-batch roasts and the best iced coffee in town.
must_try: New Orleans Iced Coffee (cold brew with chicory and milk)

name: Mojo Coffee House
description: Relaxed neighborhood coffee house in the Lower Garden District with their own excellent local roasts. Good work-from-café energy.
must_try: Pour-over coffee selections

name: Morning Call
description: Resurrected 1870s coffee stand at the end of the Canal Streetcar line near City Park. You powder the beignets yourself. A true local favorite.
must_try: Beignets (self-powder) and robust café au lait

name: PJ's Coffee
description: Louisiana-born coffee chain that locals actually drink. Reliable cold-drip iced coffee across dozens of convenient locations. Way better than Starbucks.
must_try: Original Cold Brew Iced Coffee or Velvet Ice
seasonal: King Cake flavors in early spring

name: Spitfire Coffee
address: 627 St Peter St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Precision-crafted third-wave espresso steps from Jackson Square. The best craft coffee in the French Quarter by a wide margin.
must_try: Cortado or cold brew

name: Angelo Brocato's
address: 214 N Carrollton Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Italian ice cream and pastry shop since 1905 in Mid-City. The lemon ice and cannoli are perfect. Old-world tile floors and display cases.
must_try: Lemon ice, cannoli, biscotti

name: SEIJI's OMAKASE by Little Tokyo
description: A hidden 17-seat omakase bar inside Little Tokyo in Metairie. Chef Seiji Nakano is the heart of the experience — warm, personal, and worth every penny. The top omakase in the metro.
must_try: The 7-course premium sushi-kaiseki experience ($140)
hours: Reservations required for specific nightly seatings

name: The Kingsway
description: Chef Ashwin Vilkhu's contemporary Asian tasting menu on Magazine Street. Build your own multi-course meal — scallion lamb, duck breast à l'orange, izakaya steak.
must_try: Yellowfin tuna with aged chile oil

name: Blue Oak BBQ
address: 900 N Carrollton Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Mid-City smokehouse with a distinct Louisiana profile — brisket, ribs, and boudin alongside craft beer. The patio is great.
must_try: Brisket plate with boudin and coleslaw

name: The Joint
description: Bywater institution smoking meats slow and low since 2004. Unpretentious neighborhood staple with a superb courtyard.
must_try: House-cured smoked pastrami and peanut butter pie

name: Bearcat Café
description: Popular Uptown cafe splitting the menu into 'Good Cat' (healthy/vegan) and 'Bad Cat' (indulgent). Something for everyone.
must_try: Blackberry pistachio pancakes and house-bottled teas

name: The Ruby Slipper Café
address: 315 S Broad St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Lively local brunch empire famous for decadent Southern-inspired classics and eye-opening morning cocktails. Multiple locations.
must_try: Shrimp Boogaloo Benedict and Banana Pudding Beignets

name: Toast
description: Bright quick-service cafe Uptown with hearty portions, elevated Southern comfort, and phenomenal baked goods.
must_try: Chicken and waffles with cayenne whipped butter

name: Wakin' Bakin'
description: No-frills Mid-City breakfast joint with hearty plates and a loyal local following. The kind of place where the regulars know each other.
must_try: The Sourdough King and the Pancrepes

name: A Court of Two Sisters
description: The courtyard is the star — a massive outdoor garden with a fountain, live jazz, and a spectacular brunch buffet. Enter from Bourbon or Royal.
must_try: Jazz brunch buffet — jambalaya, shrimp creole, eggs Benedict, beignets

name: The Country Club
description: Bywater gem with excellent brunch, a heated pool, and a jacuzzi in a leafy grotto. Good drinks, good food, swimsuit optional on certain days.
must_try: Bottomless brunch by the pool

name: Willa Jean
description: Kelly Fields' CBD bakery-restaurant. The cornbread with cane syrup butter is famous. Brunch and breakfast are the moves here.
must_try: Cornbread with cane syrup butter, biscuit sandwich, chocolate chip cookie (to go)

name: Cochon
description: Donald Link's love letter to Cajun country. The whole-hog ethos is real — this is nose-to-tail Southern cooking elevated to James Beard Award level.
must_try: Cochon (braised pork with turnips and cracklins), wood-fired oysters, rabbit and dumplings

name: Dooky Chase's Restaurant
description: The legendary Leah Chase fed Freedom Riders, civil rights leaders, and presidents from this Tremé kitchen. The Friday lunch buffet is a pilgrimage — fried chicken, gumbo z'herbes, and stuffed shrimp.
must_try: Fried chicken, gumbo z'herbes, stuffed shrimp. Friday lunch buffet.

name: Jacques-Imo's
description: Uptown's wildest Cajun joint. The line wraps around the block and they don't take reservations. Worth the wait for the alligator cheesecake and shrimp & alligator sausage.
must_try: Alligator cheesecake, fried chicken, shrimp & alligator sausage

name: Succotash Nola
description: New French Quarter addition where classic New Orleans cuisine meets funky neighborhood energy. 2025 opening.
must_try: The signature succotash and Gulf catches

name: Tujague's
description: The second-oldest restaurant in New Orleans (1856). Famous for the prix fixe and the stand-up bar. Old-school Creole that hasn't changed.
must_try: The prix fixe meal — brisket with Creole sauce is the signature

name: Central Grocery
description: Birthplace of the muffuletta sandwich. A half feeds two people. They wrap it to go — take it to the riverfront and eat with a view.
must_try: Original muffuletta — order a half

name: Dat Dog
description: Gourmet hot dogs and sausages — crawfish, alligator, duck. Perfect fuel between Frenchmen Street music sets. Multiple locations.
must_try: Crawfish sausage or alligator sausage with Creole mustard

name: Domilise's Po-Boy & Bar
description: Tiny Uptown shack with legendary po'boys. Cash only. The hot sausage and the fried shrimp are both devastating. You'll miss it if you're not looking.
must_try: Fried shrimp po'boy or hot sausage po'boy

name: Maspero's
description: Cheap, filling Quarter food that locals won't gatekeep. Muffulettas, po'boys, jambalaya in massive portions. Good hangover food.
must_try: Muffuletta or jambalaya

name: Parkway Bakery & Tavern
description: The po'boy that all other po'boys are measured against. Roast beef debris, gravy dripping down your arm, on perfect Leidenheimer bread. No-frills neighborhood perfection.
must_try: Roast beef debris po'boy — dressed, obviously

name: Willie Mae's Scotch House
address: 2401 St Ann St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: James Beard America's Classic. The fried chicken here has been called the best in the world — crispy, juicy, seasoned perfectly. Tremé institution since 1957.
must_try: Fried chicken. Get extra sides of butter beans and cornbread.

name: Charmant
address: 514 City Park Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Stellar 2025 Mid-City opening channeling European bistro elegance through a New Orleans lens. Date-night dinner and family-friendly brunch.
must_try: Fried Brussels Sprouts Salad and Pork Osso Bucco Arancini

name: Antoine's
address: 713 St Louis St, New Orleans, LA 70112
description: The oldest continuously operating restaurant in America (1840). Ask for a tour of the wine cellar and the Mardi Gras room. Old school French-Creole.
must_try: Oysters Rockefeller (invented here), Pompano en Papillote

name: Brennan's
description: The Royal Street institution that invented Bananas Foster. Breakfast at Brennan's is a bucket-list New Orleans experience — eggs Hussarde, turtle soup, and a tableside flambe.
must_try: Bananas Foster (invented here in 1951), eggs Hussarde, turtle soup

name: Commander's Palace
description: The grande dame of New Orleans dining. Lally Brennan's Garden District landmark has launched more chef careers than any restaurant in America. The 25-cent martini lunch is legendary.
must_try: Turtle soup, pecan-crusted Gulf fish, bread pudding soufflé. The 25¢ martini lunch on weekdays.

name: Emeril's
description: The only two-Michelin-star restaurant in the American South. E.J. Lagasse took over the kitchen in 2023 and completely reimagined the menu — it's the most buzzed-about fine dining in the city right now.
must_try: Oyster stew with Herbsaint cream, trout amandine, banana cream pie

name: Galatoire's
description: Friday lunch here is a New Orleans power ritual — jackets required downstairs, three-martini affairs that start at noon and end when they end. The dining room hasn't changed in a century.
must_try: Shrimp Remoulade, trout meunière amandine, soufflé potatoes

name: Herbsaint
address: 701 St Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Donald Link's first restaurant. French-Southern bistro cooking that's been a James Beard favorite for over two decades. The gumbo is a masterclass.
must_try: Shrimp and grits, gumbo, muscadine wine

name: Saint Claire
description: 2026 James Beard Best New Restaurant nominee in Algiers, across the river. A stunning old house with private dining rooms and a menu anchored by gnocchi with crabmeat and smoked beets.
must_try: Gnocchi with jumbo lump crabmeat, smoked beets with trout roe

name: Saint-Germain
address: 3054 St Claude Ave, New Orleans, LA 70117
description: One Michelin star. A 10-course tasting menu in a former Bywater shotgun house. The most exciting restaurant in the city — geoduck, Norwegian king crab, and caviar potato ice cream in a space that feels like a dinner party, not a temple.
must_try: The full tasting menu — it changes constantly. Trust the chefs.

name: Zasu
address: 127 N Carrollton Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: One Michelin star. Chef Sue Zemanick's Mid-City gem. Louisiana ingredients through a global lens — inventive, personal, and worth every penny.
must_try: Tasting menu with wine pairing

name: Patula
description: Tucked in a secluded Royal Street courtyard behind a boutique. Adventurous globally-inspired small plates. 2026 Resy Hit List.
must_try: Moroccan-spiced meatballs and mushroom toast

name: Saffron NOLA
description: Elegant, James Beard-nominated Indian restaurant guided by the Vilkhu family. Father of The Kingsway's chef. The cocktail program is outstanding.
must_try: Oyster bed roast and the curried seafood gumbo

name: Shaya
description: Bustling Uptown eatery marrying modern Israeli and Lebanese flavors with Gulf ingredients. The wood-fired pita alone is worth the trip.
must_try: Wood-fired pita bread and slow-cooked lamb hummus

name: Tal's Hummus
description: Relaxed counter-service cafe delivering authentic Israeli street food on Magazine Street. Fast, cheap, delicious.
must_try: Classic falafel pita and shakshuka

name: Adolfo's
description: Funky tiny cafe perched above the Apple Barrel bar on Frenchmen Street. Superb value Creole-Italian with an unbeatable location.
must_try: Any fish dish with the legendary Ocean Sauce

name: Evviva
description: Rebecca Wilcomb and Marcus Jacobs' rustic Italian spot in the Marigny. Always-changing menu, wood-fire cooking, and a glowing bar that's worth a visit on its own.
must_try: Anchovy toast, grilled shrimp, roasted mussels

name: Irene's Cuisine
description: Romantic, wildly popular French Quarter hideaway known for garlic-heavy, deeply satisfying Italian-Creole comfort food. No reservations — arrive early.
must_try: Oysters Irene and the duck St. Philip

name: Mosca's
description: Iconic roadhouse Italian on the Westbank, barely changed since the 1940s. A true culinary pilgrimage for anyone who loves garlic, family-style portions, and time-capsule restaurants.
must_try: Oysters Mosca and Chicken à la Grande

name: Barracuda
description: Ultra-casual Irish Channel taco stand and margarita garden with house-made flour tortillas. The neighborhood vibe is half the appeal.
must_try: The Farmer taco and chips with fresh guacamole

name: Johnny Sánchez
description: Aaron Sanchez and John Besh's elevated Mexican concept in the CBD. Premium tequila and mezcal program alongside upscale regional Mexican cuisine.
must_try: Table-side guacamole and the mole negro

name: Vals
description: Gorgeous renovated vintage gas station on Freret Street serving superb modern Mexican street food and an extensive agave spirits list.
must_try: Green mole chicken tacos and ceviche of the day

name: Acme Oyster House
description: Quarter institution. Sit at the marble bar and watch shuckers fly. Chargrilled oysters are the signature. Line moves fast.
must_try: Chargrilled oysters, raw dozen, shrimp po'boy

name: Delacroix
address: 1 Poydras St Spc 1005, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: The only restaurant directly on the downtown Mississippi Riverfront, offering South Louisiana classics with unmatched waterfront views. BRG Hospitality, opened September 2025.
must_try: Smoked Oyster Dip and Billy's Smoked Duck Gumbo

name: Drago's Seafood
description: The original charbroiled oysters — they invented the dish. Located in the Hilton Riverside. Not the sexiest setting but the oysters are GOAT-level.
must_try: Charbroiled oysters — the original recipe

name: Pêche Seafood Grill
description: James Beard Award winner for Best New Restaurant. Gulf seafood done over a massive wood-burning grill. The whole grilled fish is the move.
must_try: Whole grilled fish, catfish with chili glaze, crispy gulf oysters

name: Palm & Pine
address: 308 N Rampart St, New Orleans, LA 70112
description: Louisiana, the broader South, and the Caribbean collide. Agave and cane spirit cocktails meet regional ceviche. 2026 Resy Hit List.
must_try: Regional ceviche and agave cocktails

name: Studio
description: Modern Uptown steakhouse from the minds behind Doris Metropolitan. Masterful design, dry-aged cuts, decadent sides.
must_try: Dry-aged ribeye

name: Dong Phuong Bakery & Restaurant
address: 14207 Chef Menteur Hwy, New Orleans, LA 70129
description: James Beard Award-winning anchor in New Orleans East. Supplies bread for the city's best po'boy shops and serves peerless Vietnamese fare alongside legendary king cake.
must_try: Banh Mi and the seasonal Mardi Gras King Cake

name: Lilly's Café
description: Cozy Lower Garden District spot serving deeply comforting traditional Vietnamese soups and rolls.
must_try: Spicy Shrimp Pho with added quail eggs

name: Fulton Alley
description: Upscale bowling alley and prohibition-style cocktail lounge in the Warehouse District. Late-night boutique bowling.
must_try: Late-night bowling with craft cocktails

name: Fair Grounds Race Course & Slots
description: Third-oldest racetrack in America. Live thoroughbred racing Thanksgiving through March. Also the home of Jazz Fest every April/May.
must_try: Live horse racing on weekends during season, mint julep in hand

name: Harrah's New Orleans (Caesars)
description: The only land-based casino in the city. Table games, slots, sportsbook. It's no Vegas, but it's steps from the French Quarter if you want to play.
must_try: Sports betting during Saints season, blackjack tables

name: Escape My Room
description: Story-driven escape experience using authentic New Orleans history and Southern Gothic aesthetics. The best escape room in the city.
must_try: The Mardi Gras Study room

name: Orpheum Theater
description: Magnificent Beaux-Arts theater and home of the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra. Acoustically perfect.
must_try: Classical performance from the floor sweet spot

name: Saenger Theatre
description: Spectacular 1927 atmospheric theater engineered to resemble a 15th-century Italian courtyard beneath a starlit sky. Hosts major Broadway tours.
must_try: Touring Broadway musical

name: Ace Hotel New Orleans
description: Warehouse District cool in a gorgeous Art Deco building. Rooftop pool and bar, vinyl listening lounge, great lobby scene. Walking distance to everything.
must_try: Rooftop pool and bar, especially at sunset

name: Catahoula Hotel
description: Hidden 35-room CBD boutique with a great courtyard and a phenomenal Peruvian-inspired bar program. Pisco cocktails on the rooftop terrace.
must_try: Pisco cocktails on the rooftop

name: Columns Hotel
address: 3811 St Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70115
description: Majestic 1883 mansion on St. Charles Avenue. The sprawling front porch is perhaps the city's greatest place to sip a cocktail while streetcars pass.
must_try: Sazerac on the front porch watching streetcars

name: Hotel Peter and Paul
description: A converted church, school, rectory, and convent in the Marigny. Every room is different. Steps from Frenchmen Street. One of the most beautiful boutique hotels in America.
must_try: The Elysian Bar downstairs (open to non-guests) is stunning

name: Old No. 77 Hotel
description: Rustic-chic Warehouse District hotel with exposed brick and an artistic vibe. Home to Chef Nina Compton's acclaimed Compère Lapin.
must_try: Dinner at Compère Lapin downstairs

name: The Eliza Jane
description: Built inside former printing houses and bitters factories. Industrial architecture meets Parisian elegance. The library lounge is gorgeous.
must_try: Library lounge and interior courtyard

name: The Pontchartrain Hotel
address: 2031 St Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Legendary 1927 Garden District grand dame meticulously restored to mid-century glory. The rooftop bar Hot Tin has panoramic views.
must_try: Mile High Pie at the Caribbean Room and drinks at Hot Tin rooftop

name: HI New Orleans Hostel
description: Pristine modern hostel directly on Canal Street with fantastic communal spaces and budget-friendly beds. Clean, secure, perfectly located.
must_try: Mezzanine common area

name: India House Hostel
address: 124 S Lopez St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Legendary social backpacker hostel in Mid-City with a pool, communal dinners, and wild Mardi Gras parties. The budget move.
must_try: Weekly communal crawfish boils (in season)

name: Hotel Monteleone
description: The grande dame of French Quarter hotels. Family-owned since 1886. Home of the Carousel Bar. Literary history — Faulkner, Hemingway, Capote all stayed here.
must_try: Carousel Bar for a drink even if you don't stay. Rooftop pool.

name: Maison Dupuy
description: Quiet courtyard hotel in the French Quarter. Close to the music but not on top of it. Good pool, solid value for the location.
must_try: Courtyard pool area — one of the nicest in the Quarter

name: Omni Royal Orleans
address: 621 St Louis St, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Grand classic French Quarter hotel renovated in 2026. Famous rooftop pool deck overlooking the Quarter, new lobby bar and music lounge.
must_try: Rooftop pool overlooking the Quarter

name: The Roosevelt New Orleans
description: The Waldorf Astoria property. The Sazerac Bar is a must-visit (the cocktail was invented nearby). Massive rooftop pool. The lobby at Christmas is jaw-dropping.
must_try: Drink a Sazerac at the Sazerac Bar. Visit during the holidays for the lobby decorations.

name: Windsor Court Hotel
description: Old-world luxury in the CBD with an exceptional art collection, traditional afternoon tea in Le Salon, and a stunning rooftop pool.
must_try: Afternoon tea in Le Salon

name: Mississippi River Trail
address: Levee path starting at Audubon Park/The Fly
description: Flat paved multi-use path along the Mississippi River levee with stunning industrial river views and cooling breezes. Great on a Blue Bike.
must_try: Sunset cycling along The Fly behind Audubon Zoo

name: Audubon Park & Zoo
description: Beautiful oak-lined park perfect for jogging, picnicking, or the zoo. The Louisiana swamp exhibit at the zoo is excellent — real alligators, real bayou.
must_try: Walk the oak-lined path, then hit the zoo's Louisiana Swamp exhibit
hours: Park: sunrise to sunset. Zoo: Wed-Mon 10am-5pm

name: City Park
description: 1,300 acres — bigger than Central Park. Ancient live oaks draped in Spanish moss, Sculpture Garden, Besthoff Sculpture Garden (free), Storyland for kids, and the gorgeous Big Lake for paddleboating.
must_try: Besthoff Sculpture Garden (free), Café Du Monde City Park location (shorter lines), Morning Bike ride

name: Crescent Park
address: 1008 N Peters St to Mazant St, New Orleans, LA
description: Brilliant 1.4-mile linear park on the Bywater riverfront with unmatched views of the downtown skyline. Cross the Rusty Rainbow bridge at Piety Street.
must_try: The arching Rusty Rainbow bridge at Piety Street

name: Fontainebleau State Park
description: 45-minute drive across Lake Pontchartrain with sandy lake beaches, ancient moss-draped oaks, and excellent hiking. Worth the drive.
must_try: Walking the ruins of the historic sugar mill

name: Jean Lafitte National Historical Park (Barataria Preserve)
description: Free National Park just 20 minutes from downtown. Spectacular boardwalks floating over wild alligator-filled marshes. The best free outdoor experience near the city.
must_try: Visitor Center trail for birds and gators
hours: Trails open daily; Visitor Center Wed-Sun 9:30am-4:30pm

name: Woldenberg Riverfront Park
description: Brick promenade along the Mississippi right off the French Quarter. Perfect for watching massive ships pass and catching river breezes.
must_try: Watching steamboats undock at sunset

name: Cajun Encounters Swamp Tour
address: Departs from Frenier Landing, Laplace, LA (30 min from FQ)
description: The best-reviewed swamp tour near the city. See gators, turtles, herons, and cypress swamps. Most tours include hotel pickup.
must_try: The morning tour — wildlife is more active and light is better

name: Bayou Paddleboards
description: SUP rentals on Bayou St. John. Navigate the urban waterway at your own pace. Paddleboard yoga sessions available.
must_try: Paddleboard yoga sessions

name: Blue Bikes NOLA
description: Bike-share with stations everywhere. $8/24hrs with 30-min ride intervals. Great for Bywater, Marigny, City Park, and the Mississippi River Trail.
must_try: Ride from Bywater through City Park on a morning when it's not too hot

name: Rouses Market
description: Louisiana-born grocery chain with a French Quarter location. Great for stocking a rental — local hot sauces, boudin, prepared food deli, wine.
must_try: Hot food deli, local hot sauce selection, king cake (seasonal)

name: Walgreens (French Quarter)
description: The pharmacy closest to the Quarter for sunscreen, medicine, snacks, and late-night essentials.

name: Uber/Lyft (Rideshare Guide)
description: Widely available throughout the city. Typical rides: FQ to Uptown $12-18, FQ to airport $20-35. Surge pricing during festivals and events. Pickup zones at MSY airport are well-marked.

name: Ochsner Urgent Care
description: Reliable fast-service urgent care clinics throughout major tourist zones for minor medical issues and travel sickness.

name: Dirty Coast
description: Locally owned apparel brand selling high-quality gear with deep-cut New Orleans inside jokes and beautiful designs. The insider souvenir shop.
must_try: 'Expect Delays' or Water Meter merchandise

name: Fleurty Girl
description: The quintessential NOLA gift shop with locally inspired t-shirts, accessories, and home goods. Multiple locations.
must_try: Hyper-local NOLA pride t-shirts

name: Hazelnut
description: Upscale home goods boutique co-owned by actor Bryan Batt. Elegant New Orleans-themed decor and gifts.
must_try: Custom New Orleans toile ceramics

name: Magazine Street
address: Magazine St (Garden District to Audubon Park), New Orleans, LA 70115
description: Six miles of boutiques, vintage shops, galleries, and restaurants. The antithesis of a mall — walk it, stop into whatever catches your eye.
must_try: Start at Canal and walk Uptown. Funky Monkey (vintage), Trashy Diva, Hazelnut (home goods)

name: Rubenstein's
address: 102 St Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70130
description: Historic family-run luxury menswear anchor on Canal Street. Over a century of elite tailoring and service.
must_try: Custom tailoring consultation

name: French Market
address: 1235 N Peters St, New Orleans, LA 70116
description: Open-air market operating since 1791. The flea market side has souvenirs and local goods; the farmer's market side has local produce and hot sauce vendors.
must_try: Hot sauce tasting, local art, pralines

name: Frenchmen Art Bazaar
description: Nightly open-air market on Frenchmen with local art, jewelry, and one-of-a-kind New Orleans souvenirs. Way better than anything on Bourbon.
must_try: Browse between sets — paintings, mixed media, handmade jewelry

name: Faulkner House Books
description: Romantic curated bookstore in the 1837 townhouse where William Faulkner lived. Rare signed first editions of Southern literature.
must_try: Browsing rare signed first editions

name: Kitchen Witch Cookbooks
address: 1452 N Broad St, New Orleans, LA 70119
description: Eccentric bookstore dedicated entirely to culinary literature, vintage cookbooks, and regional food history. A foodie pilgrimage.
must_try: Rare out-of-print Louisiana Creole cookbooks

name: Louisiana Music Factory
description: The ultimate destination for regional jazz, blues, and zydeco on Frenchmen Street. Live in-store acoustic performances on weekends.
must_try: Weekend in-store acoustic performances

name: Peaches Records
description: Massive family-owned record store since 1975. Treasure trove for vinyl collectors — especially the local brass and bounce sections.
must_try: Digging through local brass and bounce vinyl

name: NOLA Tribe Yoga
description: Community-driven outdoor yoga beneath the ancient oaks of City Park and at local breweries. The most New Orleans fitness experience possible.
must_try: Weekend morning yoga in City Park

name: Float NOLA
description: Sensory deprivation float therapy for profound relaxation and physical recovery. The antidote to Bourbon Street.
must_try: 90-minute float tank session

name: Spa Aria at the Ritz-Carlton
description: The top-tier spa experience in the city. Indoor pool, steam room, full treatment menu. Good recovery play after a big night on Bourbon.
must_try: Couples massage or the recovery package after a long NOLA weekend

name: The Spa at Windsor Court
description: Serene old-world retreat with bespoke body treatments high above the CBD. The recovery play after a big NOLA weekend.
must_try: Monarch detoxification wrap
